chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Mus'ab Al-Hamdani, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are three matters in which no one has an excuse: paying back the trust to the righteous and to the immoral; fulfilling the covenant with the righteous and with the immoral; and being dutiful to the parents, whether they are both righteous or both immoral.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three obligations in Shia Islam that must be fulfilled even if the recipient is immoral?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of trustworthiness (adā' al-amāna) and covenant fulfillment (wafā' bi'l-'ahd) is independent of the recipient's piety, extending even to the 'fājid' (sinner). This underscores the Shia principle that these duties are objective obligations rather than reciprocal gestures, ensuring social stability regardless of individual moral standing. The inclusion of filial piety (birr al-wālidayn) even when parents are sinners highlights the enduring nature of family bonds in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Mus’ab Al Hamdany who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There are three (matters) in which no one has an excuse therein – the paying back the entrustment to the righteous as well as the immoral; and the loyalty with the covenant to the righteous as well as the immoral; and the righteousness with the parents, be they both righteous or both immoral’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Mus’ab af-Hamadaniy who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘There are three issues in which one has no choice: They are safe return of trust of a virtuous or sinful person, keeping one’s promise to a virtuous or sinful person, and kindness to parents, regardless, of their being virtuous or sinful ones.’”
